research.title: A Financial Brain Scan of the LLM
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to "brain scan" large language models, mapping internal activations to interpretable concepts and enabling targeted "steering" of specific features. We show that prompting models to adopt specific preferences activates many unintended. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Agreements Have a Clock: Compute Growth and the Verification of AI Restraint
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Rival powers have agreed to limit nuclear arms, phase out ozone-depleting chemicals, and cut greenhouse gases, though each agreement was hard to reach. This paper asks what an agreement to pause frontier AI needs. A follower. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Designing Behavioral Profiles for Language Model Simulation of Out-of-Distribution Human Behavior
research.summary: Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, but which descriptions of people improve prediction when experimental designs change remains unclear. We develop a framework that draws candidate behavioral features from the literature. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Experimentally Validated Digital Twins: Evaluating Workforce Training Programs in the Age of Big Data
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern program evaluation prioritizes evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) because prior research found that observational estimates of program impacts often diverge substantially from experimental benchmarks. We revisit this finding --- which was based on small. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: From Individual Learning to Market Equilibrium: Correcting Structural and Parametric Biases in RL Simulations of Economic Models
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to economic modeling reveals a fundamental tension: standard RL agents do not behave as competitive price-takers. While macroeconomic models typically assume agents take aggregate conditions as given, a naive single-agent RL algorithm. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Left-Digit Bias: Theory and Empirical Evidence from a Tax Salience Experiment
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Demand often drops sharply at whole-dollar prices. To explain this phenomenon, known as left-digit bias, we develop a random utility model in which consumers consider a good only if its price is below a heterogeneous attention. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Prizes, Shared Hazard, and the Speed of Frontier AI
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier AI labs compete in a contest for commercial leadership while sharing the risk of catastrophe. Each lab gains from arriving earlier but bears only part of the hazard its speed adds, which this paper calls. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: The Costs and Benefits of Leveraged ETFs
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the costs and benefits of leveraged ETFs (LETFs), focusing on five determinants of performance: volatility drag, fees, financing costs, product launches, and market timing. Long broad-equity-index LETFs generated more than 100 billion US dollars. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
